industry.size: India is the world's fourth-largest retail market, ~Rs90-95 lakh crore (~$1 trn) in CY2025, projected at ~Rs210-215 lakh crore by CY2035. Fashion and lifestyle (apparel, footwear, innerwear, beauty and personal care) was ~Rs12 lakh crore ($128 bn) in FY26 and is projected at ~Rs19 lakh crore by FY30 (~12% a year), with the organised part growing ~15% a year against ~9% for the unorganised part over FY25-30 (industry reports cited in AR FY26).
industry.categories: Beauty and personal care ~Rs2.4 lakh crore in FY26 (Rs3.8 lakh crore by FY30), footwear ~Rs1.04 lakh crore (Rs1.6 lakh crore, ~11% a year), innerwear ~Rs84,000 crore (Rs1.3 lakh crore, ~12% a year) (AR FY26). These are Trent's 'emerging categories', now over 21% of its revenue.
industry.trentShare: Trent's FY26 revenue of ~Rs20,000 crore is ~1.7% of the fashion and lifestyle market; management puts its share at ~2% (AGM 2026).
industry.competition: Value fashion is crowded: Reliance Retail (Trends, Yousta), Landmark (Max), Vishal Mega Mart (listed Dec-2024), V-Mart, Aditya Birla (Pantaloons, Style Up) and Shoppers Stop (Intune) all run value formats; Zara, H&M and Uniqlo compete at the top. Trent says it has 'not witnessed any material shifts in the competitive intensity' (Q1FY27 presentation); brokers flag domestic and international fast fashion as the main risk (ICICI Direct, 7-Aug-2026).
industry.tier2: Over 80% of new Zudio stores open in Tier II-III towns and peripheral micro-markets; Trent's own data show lower sales per sq ft outside the metros (FY26: Rs15,318 metro/Tier I, Rs13,390 Tier II, Rs12,504 rest of India) and that new markets take two to three years to mature.

excluded.ABFRL: Loss-making in every year FY20-26 and restructured by the 2025 demerger of its lifestyle brands: no P/E history to compare.
excluded.SHOPERSTOP: Net profit Rs11 cr in FY25 and a loss in FY26: the trailing P/E (~258x at 30-Sep-2026) and its five-year history are meaningless.
excluded.VMM: Vishal Mega Mart listed in Dec-2024: under two years of P/E history, no five-year median. Shown as a sensitivity row only.

peers.note: Retail peer set set by the DMART report (first retail report of the consumer-services batch): DMART, TRENT, METROBRAND, BATAINDIA, PAGEIND used; ABFRL, SHOPERSTOP and VMM excluded as stated; each report excludes itself (here TRENT, which is -47% vs its own five-year median). Sector de-rating = median of the used peers' trailing P/E at the 30-Sep-2026 close vs their five-year (Oct-2021 to Sep-2026) median, Screener data: DMart -21.8%, Metro Brands -29.1%, Bata -30.3%, Page -30.1%; median -29.6%. Sub-sets (ex-DMart, ex-Bata, ex-Metro, +VMM) give -29.1% to -30.2%.

street.note: Post-Q1FY27 targets (results 6-Aug-2026). Business Today (7-Aug-2026) puts the consensus target at Rs3,454 across 14 brokers, 13 of them Buy/Add/Neutral and one Sell. Targets are on the post-bonus share count.
street.methodSummary: The brokers that disclose a method use a sum of the parts: Westside and Zudio on ~40x pre-Ind AS EV/EBITDA (MOSL) or ~64x Sep-28E P/E (Elara), plus Star on 2-2.5x sales and the Zara/Massimo Dutti stakes on P/E. The fashion business is ~95% of each SOTP, and the overall targets equal ~58-64x FY28E EPS (MOSL 62x, Nuvama 58x at the CMP), on standalone EPS that is ~10-15% above consolidated EPS (no Star losses; dividends from the Inditex associates).

Q1FY27 results: margin beat, PAT +22%; brokers keep Buy, raise targets

moat: Own brands sold only in own stores (no wholesale, no discounting), a fast India-based supply chain, and Zudio's price points; the Tata brand helps with landlords. No pricing power: Zudio wins on price-for-quality and must keep prices stable.
critiques: Growth is bought with space: area grew ~31% in FY26 and ~33% y/y to Jun-26 while revenue grew 15-19%; like-for-like growth has been low single digit for over a year, so revenue per sq ft fell ~15% in FY26 and ~10% in Q1FY27.

New stores in smaller towns are less productive (annualised sales per sq ft Rs12,504 outside Tier I-II vs Rs15,318 in metros) and Trent opens next to its own stores: cannibalisation is a deliberate choice that the reported LFL cannot show.

Depreciation is rising faster than revenue (6.8% of revenue in FY26, 7.1% in Q1FY27, 5.2% in FY25): under Ind AS 116 rent sits below EBITDA, so EBITDA growth (+32% in Q1) overstates profit growth (+22%).
Star (THPL) is still loss-making after a decade (Rs128 cr loss before tax in FY26, wider than FY25) and part of the Rs2,500 cr raise is earmarked to roll it out faster.
A Rs2,500 cr equity raise (~1.8% of the market value) is approved but not launched: an overhang, and a sign that internal cash no longer covers every ambition.

Value fashion is getting crowded (Reliance's Yousta, Landmark's Max, Vishal, V-Mart) and quick-commerce platforms now sell basic apparel: Zudio's price advantage is harder to defend than its execution.
The stock still trades at ~53x our Sep-28E EPS after halving from its Oct-2024 peak: the street's 58-64x on FY28E assumes ~20% EPS growth for many years.

governance.note: Tata Sons controls 37% with no pledges; independent board; chairman Noel Tata retiring in Nov-2026 under the group's age-70 policy.

gaps: Trent does not disclose Westside and Zudio revenue separately, store-level economics, or a numerical LFL figure ('low single digits'). Our store build is at the level of total fashion area.

Quarterly retail area is disclosed only at some quarter ends (Jun-25 ~13.6, Mar-26 17.7, Jun-26 18.04 mn sq ft); Sep-25 and Dec-25 are interpolated on net store additions to estimate the FY26 effective area (14.84 mn sq ft).
The Q2FY26 and Q3FY26 presentations (docs.trent-tata.com) were not reachable by automated download; quarterly store counts for those quarters come from the Q4FY26 presentation's quarterly add chart.

Most post-Q1 broker targets come from press roundups (Business Today 7-Aug and 13-Aug-2026, DSIJ summaries) without the valuation method; full notes were not available to us. Elara's and Nuvama's exact note dates are not given (August 2026).
The AGM 'LFL of 11-13%' reported by Apparel Resources could not be confirmed in a company document; not used.
Consolidated cash flow 'payment of lease liabilities' (Rs797 cr) may include lease interest; we use it as cash rent in capex for the DCF.
THPL (Star) segment detail (revenue per sq ft, store-level profitability) is not disclosed; Star revenue is from presentations (excl. GST, incl. Zudio shop-in-shops).
Screener's quarterly table already shows Q2FY27 (Sep-2026, published in November); the model freezes at Q1FY27 (asOf).
conflicts: Screener's FY26 other income (Rs85 cr) differs from the reported Rs114.8 cr: Screener adds the JV/associate share (+Rs3.9 cr) and nets the labour-code exceptional (-Rs26.1 cr) and a loss on assets discarded (-Rs7.6 cr). Its FY26 finance cost (Rs233 cr) includes ~Rs64 cr of bank charges reported in other expenses.
Q1FY27 standalone revenue: Rs5,666 cr (company) vs Rs5,670 cr (Business Today rounding).
Citi's target: Rs2,950 (Business Today, 7-Aug-2026) vs Rs2,733 and Rs1,822 in other snippets that appear to be older or pre-bonus; we use Rs2,950.
Business Today (13-Aug-2026) gives DII ownership of 14.6% for Jun-2026; Screener's shareholding pattern shows 23.07%. We use Screener (exchange filing).
